title: Read a sentence and its keywords
intro: You will see a sentence and the few keywords a person typed for it. Answer four short questions about the words on the page.
Questions 1 and 2 are about the sentence. Questions 3 and 4 are about the keywords only: ignore the sentence for those two.

help.text: statement tells something (including 'I want tea.'). question asks for information or permission. request/command asks someone to do something. other if none of these fits.
polite if it has please, thank you, sorry, excuse me, could you, would you or a similar polite or softened form.
For questions 3 and 4, look only at the keywords. Would a reader of the keywords alone already know it is a question or request (or polite)? Words like 'where', 'can you', 'please' would show it.

q2.title: Is the sentence polite?
q2.text: Please, thank you, sorry, softened wording like 'could you'.

q3.title: Keywords only: a question or request?
q3.text: Look ONLY at the keywords. Do the keywords by themselves already show a question or a request (not a plain statement)?

q4.title: Keywords only: polite?
q4.text: Look ONLY at the keywords. Do the keywords by themselves already show politeness?
